# OpenCodeStatusPlugin [![CI](https://github.com/hamster007Github/OpenCodeStatusPlugin/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hamster007Github/OpenCodeStatusPlugin/actions/workflows/ci.yml) Provider status for OpenCode Go, inside OpenCode Desktop. OpenCode Go can degrade or go down in the middle of a session, and nothing in the desktop app tells you. This plugin polls the official OpenCode status feed and shows the parts you care about — Go and its models — where you already look: a compact pill above the composer, a side panel with the detail, and a settings page that decides what is shown. ## What it shows | Surface | Content | | --- | --- | | Composer pill | One line: `OpenCode [scope] mark` — `OpenCode [Go] 🟢` operational, `OpenCode [Go] 🟡` degraded, `OpenCode [Go] 🔴` outage, `OpenCode [Go] ❔️` unknown or stale. Its menu lists the watched services with their state and reason, and opens the panel. | | Side panel | Per-service and per-model state with the reason (`errors`, `upstream`, `latency`, `availability`), the time since the current state began, median time to first token and tokens per second, ongoing incidents with their latest update, the 7-day history strip, the age of the last check, and a stale warning. | | Settings page | Which services and models are watched, whether speed, incidents and history are shown, and when the plugin may notify. | | CLI/TUI | Footer mark `[Go] 🟢` — the desktop pill without the `OpenCode` prefix, because terminal width is limited — in both the home footer and the session prompt footer (each can be turned off) and `/provider-status`, which lists the watched services and drills into their models. Incidents are one more entry. | | Command | `provider-status.open` opens the panel from the command palette. The side panel's **+** menu lists it too. | The pill is one line: the product, the watched scope and a mark. It never carries a number, a unit or a model id: those need room, a baseline and a unit, and they live in the panel. Deliberately not shown: - **Models in the pill menu.** A model's state means little without its reason and speed, and the panel shows both with units. The menu answers "which service is not healthy" and gets out of the way. - **Per-service history strips.** One strip for the watched scope answers "was it like this before?"; six would double the panel and repeat the answer. - **Resolved incidents.** The 7-day strip covers the past. The status page keeps the full list, and the panel links to it. - **The feed's overall `status`.** It counts services the user does not watch. The pill and the panel derive their state from the watched scope only, so a free-tier outage does not alarm a Go user. ## Screenshots **Desktop.** The pill sits above the composer and answers one question in one line — which scope, which state. The arrow marks what this plugin adds to the app. The panel behind it carries the detail: per service and per model, with the reason, the time since the state began, median time to first token, tokens per second, ongoing incidents and the 7-day strip. **CLI.** The footer mark is the pill's scope and mark without the `OpenCode` prefix, because terminal width is limited. The arrow marks it; `5.3K (1%)` and `ctrl+p commands` belong to the app. `/provider-status` is the panel's terminal counterpart: ## Severity One scale, used by every surface: | State | Pill mark | Reads as | | --- | --- | --- | | `operational` | 🟢 green | nothing to do | | `degraded` | 🟡 yellow | slower or partly failing | | `outage` | 🔴 red | not usable | | `unknown` | `❔️` | the plugin does not know | | stale | `❔️` | the data is old | The pill shows the mark only; the words are in its accessible name, its menu rows and the panel, so colour is reinforcement and never the only signal. `unknown` and stale data never use the green mark. Each mark is configuration (`lights`), so the pill can show words or another symbol set instead. ## Data source [`https://status.opencode.ai/api/status`](https://status.opencode.ai/api/status) is the JSON snapshot behind . It is public, needs no key and is cached by the origin for 15 seconds. The endpoint sends no CORS header, so a browser window cannot call it directly. The plugin's server part polls and caches it, and the GUI reads that cache over RPC: one request per OpenCode server, not one per window. The desktop app's own server holds the cache for every window, so a session on another OpenCode server reads the same status; that server does not need the plugin. The status page's HTML is never parsed. Every field, the service and reason enumerations, the speed units, the history buckets and the staleness rules are documented in [`docs/status-feed.md`](https://github.com/hamster007Github/OpenCodeStatusPlugin/blob/main/docs/status-feed.md). ## Requirements - OpenCode Desktop 2.x. The GUI plugin API is experimental and may change between releases. - OpenCode 2.x for the CLI/TUI part. The same global plugin entry loads it; no separate `cli.json` entry is needed because the package has a server part. - This build was made against `@opencode/plugin` **2.2.5**. - The plugin listed in the **global** `opencode.jsonc`: the desktop app reads plugins only from the server it runs, and a plugin's GUI reaches every window only when it is configured globally. - For development: Bun 1.x. ## Platforms Windows, macOS and Linux. The plugin has no native code: the server part is one `fetch` plus the app's APIs, and the GUI is a single JavaScript bundle the app loads. | Platform | Status | | --- | --- | | Windows | developed and verified here: pill, panel, settings page, live feed; CI verifies the build and tests | | Linux, macOS | CI verifies the build and tests on Ubuntu and macOS; a load in the desktop app is not yet verified | Notes: - The global config lives at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/opencode.json(c)`) on every platform. - Linux needs a colour emoji font (Noto Color Emoji is standard on desktop distributions) for the default marks. Without one, set `lights` to text, for example `{"operational":"OK","degraded":"WARN","outage":"DOWN","unknown":"?","stale":"?"}`. - Notifications follow the app's notification settings and need a notification daemon on Linux. ## Install Add it to the **global** config, with the command or by editing the file: ```sh opencode plugin add opencode-status-plugin ``` ```jsonc // ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc { "plugins": ["opencode-status-plugin"], } ``` The CLI reads the same global entry. No `cli.json` change is needed for this package because it has a server part; `cli.json` is for packages with only a TUI part. For local development, point your **global** config at this folder: ```jsonc // ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc { "plugins": [{ "package": "C:/path/to/OpenCodeStatusPlugin", "options": { "services": ["go"] } }], } ``` List the plugin in one place only. A second entry in the project config loads another instance with the same id, and the desktop app reports the plugin as failed. ## Update A configured plugin does not update itself. OpenCode checks unpinned npm plugins when its server starts, but it keeps the installed version until you ask it to update: ```sh opencode plugin check # is anything outdated? opencode plugin update # every outdated package plugin opencode plugin update opencode-status-plugin # just this one opencode plugin list # what is installed ``` An entry pinned to an exact version (`"opencode-status-plugin@0.1.1"`) is skipped by both commands: drop the version, or run `opencode plugin add opencode-status-plugin@0.2.0`. A local path is never updated by the CLI, because you edit that directory yourself. Plugin changes reload without a restart. If the server part still reports the old version, restart the shared service and check it: ```sh opencode service restart opencode service status ``` In Desktop, **Settings → Extensions → Plugins** shows the installed version, and its **Reload** button loads a plugin again after a failed start. The per-plugin switch there only hides the desktop UI; to turn the plugin off entirely, add `"-provider-status"` to `plugins`. ## Configuration Options are passed in the plugin entry. OpenCode reloads the plugin when they change. | Option | Default | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `services` | `["go"]` | Services to watch: `console`, `logs`, `inference`, `go`, `payg`, `free`. Unknown names are dropped; an empty result falls back to `go`. | | `models` | `"all"` | `"all"`, or an array of model ids to watch within the selected services. `[]` means `"all"`. | | `showSpeed` | `true` | Show median time to first token and tokens per second in the panel. | | `showIncidents` | `true` | Show ongoing incidents and their latest update. | | `showHistory` | `true` | Show the 7-day history strip in the panel. | | `intervalSeconds` | `60` | Poll interval, clamped to 30–3600 seconds. The origin caches for 15 seconds, so faster buys nothing. | | `staleAfterSeconds` | `180` | Age at which a snapshot is stale, clamped to at least the poll interval. | | `notify` | `"off"` | `"off"`, `"degraded"` or `"outage"`: a system notification when the watched scope reaches that state. | | `tuiHomeFooter` | `true` | Show the status mark in the CLI home footer. | | `tuiPromptFooter` | `true` | Show it in the session prompt footer as well. | | `tuiNotify` | `"off"` | `"off"`, `"degraded"` or `"outage"`: a terminal notification for the watched scope. Separate from `notify`. | | `apiUrl` | the official endpoint | Override for testing against a mirror. HTTPS only, or plain HTTP on `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`. | | `lights` | `{"operational": "🟢",`
`"degraded": "🟡",`
`"outage": "🔴",`
`"unknown": "❔️",`
`"stale": "❔️"}` | The mark the pill shows for each state. Any text or symbol works; `stale` covers old data. | ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "opencode-status-plugin", "options": { "services": ["go", "inference"], "models": ["deepseek-v4.1-flash", "glm-5.3-flash"], "showSpeed": true, "notify": "outage", "tuiPromptFooter": true, "tuiNotify": "degraded", "lights": { "degraded": "WARN", "outage": "DOWN" } } } ], } ``` **Settings → Extensions → Provider status** edits the same scope, switches and pill marks per app, and takes precedence over the options. The settings store holds overrides only: a field you never touched stays absent, so a changed option still applies. At least one service and one model always stay watched. Notifications are opt-in. They are limited to the watched scope, and the app deduplicates them by event id, so several open windows notify once. The CLI reads the plugin options only. Its footer placement and notification level are not part of the desktop settings store; set `tuiHomeFooter`, `tuiPromptFooter` and `tuiNotify` in the plugin entry. The CLI copy is English-only in this version. The CLI has two footer slots: `home.footer.status` on the start screen, and `prompt.footer.status` inside a session. If OpenCode restores a session on launch, you are not on the home screen; close its tab (`Ctrl+X`, then `W`) to get back to home. Both slots show the same `[Go] 🟢` mark once the first status read has answered. ## How it works ```text status.opencode.ai/api/status │ poll + validate + cache (server part, one per OpenCode server) ▼ RPC `provider-status`: snapshot, refresh, changed │ ├── GUI (window) ── composer pill, side panel, settings page, command └── TUI (terminal) ── footer mark, /provider-status service and model list ``` - `src/index.ts` — server part: the poller, the last-good cache, the RPC registration and the `changed` event. - `src/rpc.ts` — the RPC contract (`opencode-status-plugin/rpc`), shared by both sides. - `src/gui.tsx` — the `./gui-experimental` entry. - `src/gui/` — window setup, pill, panel, settings page, store and the panel styles. - `src/tui.tsx` — the `./tui` entry. - `src/tui/` — CLI controller, footer mark, detail dialogs, notifications and copy. - `src/copy.ts` — translator-based labels shared by the GUI and the CLI. - `src/status/` — the status domain: types, fetch, parsing, watched-scope selectors, formatting and the shared severity mark. Facts the code keeps: - **The server caches a bounded snapshot, the window applies the scope.** The settings page changes the watched scope without reloading the server, so the server cannot be the only place that knows it. The cache keeps every service in the feed, the ongoing incidents and 56 history buckets; the window narrows that to the scope it reads from the store and the options, through the same selector on both sides. - **The payload is untrusted.** Unknown states, unknown reasons, missing fields and non-numeric speeds degrade to `unknown` or to no value. A response that does not look like a status document keeps the previous cache and marks the view stale. - **Neither surface has a timer.** The window reads the cache when a session is routed, on every `changed` event (one per successful poll, so a window that missed a transition still catches up), and when the panel is focused. The CLI reads on setup, on every `changed` event, and when its refresh command runs. A refresh asks the server to poll; the poller coalesces a burst of clicks. - **The origin's model list is `breakdown[]`.** `models[]` exists but is empty; both are read so a change upstream does not blank the panel. ## Development ```sh bun install # creates bun.lock; commit it bun run typecheck bun test bun run build # emits dist/gui-experimental.cjs bun run dev # vite build --watch: rebuilds and reloads the GUI on every change ``` Load the plugin from this folder in a global config (see Install), then open **Settings → Extensions → Plugins** and check that it loaded. The server part does not hot-reload; the GUI does. The bundle is one CommonJS file built with the `gui()` preset. Modules the app provides — `effect`, `solid-js`, `@opencode/plugin/gui` and the rest — stay external, and the app's own components come from `ctx.ui`. The TUI part is loaded from `./src/tui.tsx`; it has no separate bundle. Run `opencode` with the plugin in the global config to see the footer and `/provider-status`. ### Live API check `bun run check:api` fetches the live endpoint and passes the response through the same `fetchStatus` → `parsePayload` → `scopeStatus` path the server uses. It reports contract drift and exits: - `0` when the shape holds, or when the endpoint or the network is unreachable (inconclusive), - `1` only when the endpoint answers with a payload that no longer matches the contract. A scheduled **API contract** workflow runs it daily and on demand. It is deliberately separate from pull request CI: a status outage or a GitHub network problem must never block a change. ## Releasing The version lives in `package.json` and must be bumped for every publish, because npm refuses a duplicate version. Notes go in `CHANGELOG.md`; the full runbook is [`docs/releasing.md`](https://github.com/hamster007Github/OpenCodeStatusPlugin/blob/main/docs/releasing.md). ```sh bun run typecheck && bun test && bun run build && bun run check:api bun pm pack --dry-run # the tarball: src, dist, README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG ``` Publishing needs npm ≥ 11.15 and Node ≥ 22.14. The maintainer account uses a security key as its second factor, so a release goes through `npm stage publish` and an approval in the browser instead of a terminal one-time password; later releases run in the manual **Publish** workflow with npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC). Both paths, the trusted-publisher setup, the tarball smoke test and the post-publish checks are in [`docs/releasing.md`](https://github.com/hamster007Github/OpenCodeStatusPlugin/blob/main/docs/releasing.md). ## Not yet verified - [ ] A load in OpenCode Desktop on Linux or macOS - [ ] A load of the TUI part in the OpenCode CLI - [ ] A load of the published npm package in OpenCode, on any platform ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. Keep the payload handling defensive, keep the pill compact, and run `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` before opening a pull request. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/hamster007Github/OpenCodeStatusPlugin/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/hamster007Github/OpenCodeStatusPlugin/blob/main/SECURITY.md) and [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/hamster007Github/OpenCodeStatusPlugin/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). The feed contract is in [`docs/status-feed.md`](https://github.com/hamster007Github/OpenCodeStatusPlugin/blob/main/docs/status-feed.md), the release runbook in [`docs/releasing.md`](https://github.com/hamster007Github/OpenCodeStatusPlugin/blob/main/docs/releasing.md). ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](https://github.com/hamster007Github/OpenCodeStatusPlugin/blob/main/LICENSE).

# Changelog

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project
follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## Unreleased

## [0.1.1] - 2026-11-27

### Added

- The README shows screenshots of the pill, the panel, the CLI footer and `/provider-status`; the
  pill and the footer mark which part the plugin adds to the app.
- The README has an **Update** section: `opencode plugin check`, `opencode plugin update`, what an
  exact pinned version skips, and the service restart and Desktop reload when the old version stays
  loaded.

### Changed

- The repository is public, so the **Publish** workflow relies on the provenance that trusted
  publishing generates automatically; the release notes no longer explain a private-repository
  exception.
- Documentation: the feed contract moved to `docs/status-feed.md` and the release steps to
  `docs/releasing.md`. The README is user-facing again, section titles name what they contain, and
  every fact has a single home instead of being repeated across the README, `AGENTS.md` and
  `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

### Fixed

- A desktop window in a remote project sent that project's location to the app's own server, which
  rejected the unknown directory. The window now reads the app-wide cache without a location, so a
  session on another OpenCode server works even when that server does not load the plugin.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-11-08

### Added

- CI verifies the plugin on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS.
- A daily **API contract** workflow feeds the live status payload through the plugin's own fetch,
  parser and scope selector. It fails only on a schema change and treats an unreachable endpoint or
  a network problem as inconclusive. `bun run check:api` runs the same check locally.
- CLI/TUI: a footer mark with the desktop pill's scope and mark but without the `OpenCode` prefix,
  in both the home and prompt footers (`tuiHomeFooter`, `tuiPromptFooter`, both on by default), and
  `/provider-status`, which lists the watched services and drills into their models. `tuiNotify` adds
  opt-in terminal notifications. Both read the same server cache over RPC; the CLI copy is
  English-only in this version.
